objective: Test whether a supplied photo is stronger when important elements are extracted and recomposed into the cover instead of being used as a full rectangular image field.

preserved_identity_anchors: long dark hair, white floral dress, and pose
dense green leaves and palm fronds

changed_method: full-photo field → extracted person and selected leaf silhouettes
plain text over photo → title shares halftone/overprint and contour structure with extracted elements
photo-only background → skill gradient-first background with photo-derived subject layers

locked_recipe.composition_sentence: TITLE_MASS + SINGLE_OBJECT + IMAGE_MASK + NEGATIVE_SPACE_CUT + RELEASE_ZONE + SHARED_ALIGNMENT

visual_checks.photo_extraction: PASS — person and selected foliage become separate graphic subject layers; the full rectangular photo is not used
visual_checks.title_image_fusion: PASS — title shares color separation, halftone texture, and contour relationships with the extracted figure and leaves
visual_checks.title_first: PASS — title is first at full size and approximately 25% thumbnail
visual_checks.mask_behavior: PASS — one shaped low-detail cut releases the title without covering the face or torso
visual_checks.gradient_background: PASS — continuous warm-ivory/pistachio/apricot atmospheric field remains visible behind the extracted subject
visual_checks.photographic_identity: PASS — face, pose, dress, and green-leaf context remain recognizable

observed_evidence: The woman is a recognizable halftone/duotone figure rather than a full photo rectangle.
Large palm fronds are retained as deliberate green graphic silhouettes and partially overlap the title field.
The title is visually printed into the same image system through overprint and shared texture, not placed in a plain text box.
The background gradient fills the entire canvas and remains an active compositional layer.
The title, figure, foliage, and mask form one subject-image system at thumbnail scale.
interpretation: This proof supports an extraction-first source-asset workflow for IMAGE_MASK_FIELD. It is materially stronger than the previous full-photo-plus-overlay proof, but one image does not establish reliability across supplied photos.
candidate_skill_rules: Before choosing composition, decompose every supplied photo into 2–4 identity anchors and selected subject layers.
Use the extracted layers as the subject mass; do not default to the full rectangular photo as the background.
Require title and image layers to share an edge, contour, color plate, halftone, or overprint relationship; reject plain overlay treatment.
Rebuild the continuous skill gradient behind and between extracted layers so source imagery does not replace the gradient system.
Keep identity anchors protected while allowing nonessential background detail to be discarded or abstracted.
next_step: Run repeated IMAGE_MASK_FIELD tests across portrait, scene, and low-contrast supplied photos before centralizing these rules in SKILL.md.
